newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish Merita Bank profit up 93 pct.
newsitem.headline: Finnish Merita Bank profit up 93 pct.

text.p: Finland's biggest banking group Merita Oy said on Thursday its January-September operating profit after credit losses rose 93 percent to 930 million markka ($205 million) from 482 million in the same period last year.

Merita attributed the earnings growth, squarely in line with analysts forecasts, to a significant decline in non-performing loans and credit losses, steady performance in its core banking business, disposal of assets and lower costs.

Nine-month earnings per share rose to 0.98 markka from 0.61 markka, and the bank said it aimed to pay a dividend on its preferential B shares and a modest dividend also on its A shares out of 1996 earnings.

It would be the first time in five years that shareholders would enjoy a dividend. Of the banking groups that merged to form Merita in 1995, Unitas last paid a dividend on its 1991 result and Kansallis-Osake-Pankki in 1990.
Merita group net income from financial operations rose to 3,026 million markka from 2,756 million.
Net income from securities trading grew to 873 million markka from 399 million.
Loan losses were down to 1,144 million markka from 1,443 million. "The trend in loan losses has been more favourable than expected," Merita said in a statement with its results.
Merita said the merger process had progressed as planned or even ahead of schedule and that the full impact of merger-related cost savings would be felt next year.
The bank repeated an earlier forecast that it had good chances for a clearly positive result in 1996 and said there were chances for further improvement next year.
